projects.title: Data Integrity, Forensic Verification & Contract Audit
projects.purpose: Audit schema, evaluate contract invariants, and expose synthetic generator artifacts in merchant coordinates.
objectives: Validate schema definitions and detect identifier leaks (trans_num, cc_num).
Expose coordinate jitter forensics in merchant locations (non-physical distance signal).
Establish baseline class imbalance across train and test temporal splits.
projects.riskNote: Generator jitter artifacts in merchant coordinates create artificial discriminative signals.
limitations: Raw source datasets (fraudTrain.csv, fraudTest.csv) are not in the local workspace.
Merchant coordinates represent per-transaction jitter, not physical store geography.

topFindings.title: Class imbalance: train 7506/1296675 = 0.5789%, test 2145/555719 = 0.3860% — extreme imbalance, drift between splits detected
Temporal split: train ends 2020-06-21 12:13:37, test starts 2020-06-21 12:14:25 — time-series CV is REQUIRED for any modeling (walk-forward implemented in §08)
Schema audited; identifiers (cc_num/zip/trans_num) excluded from numeric analyses
999 cards × ~1,471 median txns — repeated-measures structure ⇒ card-clustered inference (§06) is mandatory

projects.title: Behavioral Patterns, Multi-Way Interactions & Temporal Dynamics
projects.purpose: Map univariate, bivariate and multi-way risk concentration across categories, amounts, cardholder history and temporal cycles.
objectives: Characterize amount distributions, right-tail skew, and non-linear risk escalation.
Quantify category × hour of day interactions (e.g. night online shopping risk).
Decompose temporal series with STL (seasonality, day-of-week periodicity, change points).

keyMetric.label: Night Interaction Risk
keyMetric.interpretation: Risk multiplier for night + risky categories + amt ≥ $500

projects.riskNote: Card-level fraud incidence in simulator (97.7%) is opposite of production fraud concentration.
deliverables: STL time-series decomposition and autocorrelation profiles
limitations: Card-level fraud incidence is an artifact of the simulator's per-card allocation.
Structural breaks are driven by simulation campaigns rather than real calendar holidays.

topFindings.title: Fraud amounts are strongly shifted right vs non-fraud (see §06 effect sizes: Cliff's delta with bootstrap CI)
Night hours (00–06) show markedly elevated fraud rate vs volume share (see phase1_hour figure + §06 forest plot with CIs)
Category × hour interaction: online-shopping-type categories concentrate fraud in the 22:00–06:00 window (see heatmap)
Per-card fraud rate is bimodal: 2.3% of cards never defrauded, 97.7% defrauded at least once — fraud is card-clustered, not exchangeable across transactions

projects.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection & Manifold Representations
projects.purpose: Evaluate whether fraud separates from genuine transactions in low-dimensional embeddings and unsupervised outlier detection.
objectives: Test 2D manifold projections (PCA, UMAP, t-SNE) for class separability.
Measure clustering stability using K-Means and DBSCAN density clustering.
Benchmark unsupervised detectors: Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), Autoencoders.
projects.riskNote: High false positive rate under extreme class imbalance without behavioral card history.
deliverables: Cluster purity and fraud density analysis
limitations: LOF evaluated on 5,000 transaction subsample due to quadratic distance complexity.
Unsupervised geometry reflects transaction volume density rather than fraud clusters.

topFindings.title: Unsupervised anomaly detection isolates fraud only weakly (AUCs 0.731–0.881): fraud is contextual relative to card history, not pointwise-outlying — motivates per-card features (§07)
Embedding separability: best = PCA(2) (logistic AUC 0.816); embeddings show partial fraud structure but no clean separation — consistent with noisy-overlap fraud signatures
K-Means (k=3): densest cluster reaches 1.9× baseline fraud rate — clusters capture some risk structure but no pure-fraud cluster
Clustering stability: hierarchical vs K-Means ARI = 0.74; DBSCAN finds 1 clusters + 4% noise — structure is dominated by volume, not by fraud

projects.title: Inferential Statistics, Non-Parametric Effect Sizes & Clustered Inference
projects.purpose: Establish robust, non-parametric effect sizes with bootstrap intervals and control for repeated cardholder transaction clustering.
objectives: Compute Cliff's delta and Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance with 95% bootstrap intervals.
Construct forest plots with Wilson confidence intervals and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control.
Fit cluster-robust logit with card-level clusters to evaluate repeated-measures shrinkage.

keyMetric.label: Amount Cliff's Delta
keyMetric.interpretation: Statistically robust rightward fraud amount shift

projects.riskNote: Rigorous inference; repeated-measures adjustments prevent over-claiming per-transaction effects.
deliverables: Non-parametric effect size catalogue with bootstrap CIs
Category rate forest plot with Wilson intervals
limitations: Single-seed synthetic simulation limits cross-environment generalization.
Statistical significance does not equal operational cost-effectiveness.

topFindings.title: Amount shift quantified: Cliff's delta = 0.669 [bootstrap CI 0.656, 0.680], KS D = 0.724 [0.715, 0.732], BH-q = 0
Categorical associations with target: category V=0.067 > state > gender — effect sizes (not just p) reported per plan §7.2
Hour forest: night hours carry statistically robust rate elevations (Wilson CIs exclude baseline after BH correction)
Category forest identifies the high-risk merchant categories with CIs — the forest plot is the primary evidence table for categorical risk

projects.title: Behavioral Feature Engineering, Leak-Aware Encodings & Survival Dynamics
projects.purpose: Engineer leak-aware velocity features, cyclical temporal transforms, empirical Bayes shrinkage, and hazard models.
objectives: Formulate causal expanding target encodings without future-to-past leakage.
Construct trailing velocity counters, cumulative spend, and implied travel speeds.
Model discrete-time fraud arrival hazard across customer account lifecycle.
projects.riskNote: Expanding priors strictly respect causality; naive encodings leak future labels.
deliverables: Target encoding causality proof and leakage demonstration
Discrete-time hazard curves and cohort retention tables
limitations: Implied speed features depend on coordinate jitter noise rather than actual customer mobility.
Expanding window features induce severe distribution shift across long temporal horizons.

topFindings.title: Velocity features are the strongest behavioral signals: fraud rate rises monotonically with implied speed and with trailing-window counts (see next figure)
Leakage demo: naive group-mean TE correlates with the test target at ρ=0.048 vs causal ρ=0.048 — every published pipeline using full-data target encodings on this dataset overstates its signal
Interaction check: night + risky categories + amt≥500 multiplies risk 42× vs baseline — interactions materially beat main effects (SHAP interactions in §08 for the model view)
Repeated-fraud: 0.0% of affected cards experience ≥2 distinct fraud events; event-size distribution shows bursty multi-txn compromises rather than persistent re-fraud

projects.title: Supervised Modeling, Decomposed Ablation & Out-of-Domain Transfer
projects.purpose: Train causal leak-free LightGBM, quantify out-of-domain transfer collapse, and isolate drift mechanisms via ablation.
objectives: Train baseline leak-free LightGBM classifier with early stopping.
Conduct walk-forward time-ordered cross-validation (4 folds) for honest generalization.
Decompose ablation: isolate card_prior_fraud as the primary driver of OOD transfer failure.
Perform adversarial validation (AUC = 1.000) and PSI feature drift ranking.

keyMetric.label: In-Domain vs OOD Gap
keyMetric.interpretation: 0.9510 in-domain vs 0.473 test score across folds

projects.riskNote: Adversarial validation separates train and test perfectly (AUC = 1.000) via cumulative features.
limitations: Single-seed experiment lacks variance bounds for hyperparameter tuning.
Cumulative velocity features do not transfer across temporal split boundaries.

topFindings.title: Adversarial validation achieves held-out AUC = 1.000 (FIX #3) — train and test are (near-)perfectly separable by cumulative-history features (top: te_category, te_state, n_prior). Every train→test metric in this notebook (final PR-AUC, ablation delta, learning curve) measures out-of-distribution transfer under temporal drift, NOT typical generalization; walk-forward CV within the train period is the honest generalization estimate, and the ablation / learning-curve deltas must be read through this OOD lens

PSI per feature confirms which features drive the AUC=1.000 adversarial split: 7 of 27 features are SEVERE (PSI≥0.25) — top: month_sin=6.51, n_prior=5.10, month_cos=1.45. This corroborates the ablation: expanding target encodings and cumulative-history counts carry the train/test drift, so their within-model weight is a drift signal rather than a fraud signal
Walk-forward CV (time-ordered, 4 folds): PR-AUC 0.9510 ± 0.0152 — single-carve-out estimates would understate variance (review rigor item)

OOD transfer quantified (FIX #10): the SAME fold models score PR-AUC 0.951±0.015 in-domain but 0.473±0.076 on the held-out test split — mean OOD gap = +0.478 per fold. This is the cleanest single number for 'within-train generalisation minus cross-boundary transfer' and should be cited whenever anyone quotes a single train→test metric on this dataset

projects.title: Decision Policy Economics, Operating Thresholds & Dollar Capture
projects.purpose: Optimize review operating thresholds under variable friction costs ($1–$50 FP) and evaluate capture@k budget curves.
objectives: Derive cost-sensitive operating thresholds minimizing expected total financial loss.
Evaluate review budget capacity: dollar capture and event recall at 1%–5% review bandwidth.
Audit segment-level error distributions and financial exposure trade-offs.

keyMetric.label: Capture @ 1% Budget
keyMetric.interpretation: Captures 65.5% fraud events, 68.7% dollars in top 1% reviews

projects.riskNote: Optimal operating point swings 443× depending on friction cost per review ($1 vs $50).
deliverables: Cost-sensitivity frontier and segment error diagnostics
limitations: Assumes static $5 baseline review friction cost without model retraining.
Excludes downstream customer friction, merchant dispute costs, and investigator queue latency.

topFindings.title: Cost-sensitive operating point: threshold 0.0000 minimizes expected loss (FP $5 friction vs full fraud amount) — recall 0.842 with $92,044 missed
Review budget: flagging top 1% of test by score captures 65.5% of fraud events and 68.7% of fraud dollars

Cost sensitivity (FIX #12): the cost-min threshold is fragile under FP-cost assumptions from $1 to $50 (threshold ratio 443.6×, optimal thresholds 0.0000–0.0004) — 70.2%–91.6% recall range across the sweep
Segment errors at the operating point: weakest recall in health_fitness, kids_pets, personal_care — where fraud is rare or amounts are small (see table for state/hour breakdowns)
